query: How will we define network ties and exposure mappings (supplier/customer, ownership, geographic proximity), set measurement protocols and exposure thresholds, and specify contingency rules for incomplete network data?

response.query: How will we define network ties and exposure mappings (supplier/customer, ownership, geographic proximity), set measurement protocols and exposure thresholds, and specify contingency rules for incomplete network data?
response.answer: Network ties define relationships between entities, while exposure mappings track supplier/customer, ownership, and geographic proximity. Measurement protocols establish criteria for data collection, and exposure thresholds set limits for risk assessment. Contingency rules address incomplete data with alternative methods or assumptions.

results.title: Bharat Bhraman Yatra
results.content: Throughout history, the Ashwamedha Yagya has been performed by various prominent kings and emperors in ancient India, particularly from the Vedic period to the classical age. While the Ashwamedha Yagya was a major event in ancient times, its performance has become increasingly rare in modern India. | 1.Assess venue to determine intention, motive of the gathering | 1.Don’t allow the event to happen if crowd management preparedness is found wanting in either of the area of fire prevention, adherence to structural safety, electricity, hygiene, medical, traffic etc. | 2.Help venue/event manager develop crowd management plan | 2.dont ignore the local economic activities around the venue and possible impact of displacement |
